status: Draft written by Claude from Dasha's method; Dasha edits it. The app's AI picks and personalizes entries from this file and never invents advice outside it in v1.
principles: The data shows where money leaks, not why. Never state a cause: ask, then propose a test.
Plain words only. No LTV, CAC, churn, AOV or conversion rate in anything the seller reads.
Every concept gets one line on why it matters: teach by doing.
One test at a time, with a number that says whether it worked.
Say what is fine and can be left alone, so the seller stops spending time there.
placeholders: Filled by the engine, never by the model: {past_buyers}, {month_buyers}, {top_group}, {item}, {small_group}, {n_unpaid}, {unpaid_total}, {threshold}, {small_share}, {target_share}, {target_orders}, {target_paid}, {target_rate}, {new_share}, {last_new}, {target_new}, {break_even_price}, {n_failed}, {target}
fine_rule: A monthly leak under 2% of average monthly sales is shown as: small, leave it for now.

leaks.name: Most buyers buy once
leaks.why: Someone who already bought from you trusts you. Selling to them again needs no ads and no searching, so it is the cheapest sale you can make.

questions.text: Can you reach people who bought before?

answers.text: Yes, they follow me or joined my list

questions.text: How often do you have something new?

tests.do: Show your newest {top_group} to the past buyers who follow you, with a small thank-you for returning buyers (for example free shipping).
tests.success: {target_orders} orders from past buyers within 14 days
tests.target_rule: max(1, round(past_buyers * 0.03)); halve it for answer 'some'

tests.do: Make one add-on that goes with your best seller ({top_group}) and offer it first to past buyers who follow you.
tests.target_rule: max(1, round(past_buyers * 0.03)); halve it for answer 'some'

tests.do: From today, put a small card in every order inviting buyers to follow you or join your list for new pieces.
tests.success: Half of this month's {month_buyers} buyers can be reached again

leaks.name: Money waiting in unpaid invoices
leaks.why: An invoice nobody chases often just sits there. A polite reminder is the easiest money you can make this month.

tests.do: Send a reminder for the {n_unpaid} invoices unpaid for 14+ days. On your next custom order, ask for a deposit up front.

paypal_action.label: Send reminders in PayPal
paypal_action.approval: one Approve per invoice, or one Approve for the listed set

paypal_action.label: Ask for a deposit on a custom order

leaks.name: One item keeps coming back
leaks.why: A refund loses the sale and usually costs you more on top: fees, shipping and your time.

questions.text: Why do people send back your {item}?

tests.do: Add a simple size guide to the {item} listing and confirm the size with the buyer before you ship.
Reshoot the {item} in daylight and add one photo of it being worn.
Change how you pack the {item} for the next 10 orders.
tests.success: No damaged {item} in the next 10 orders

tests.do: Ask the next 3 people who send back the {item} one question: what was wrong?

leaks.name: Fees eat your small orders
leaks.why: PayPal takes a fixed amount on every payment, on top of a percentage. On a cheap item that fixed part is a big slice.

questions.text: Could your cheapest items sell as a set?

tests.do: Offer {small_group} as a set of two at a small discount.
tests.success: Orders under {threshold}: from {small_share}% to {target_share}% of orders

tests.do: Set a minimum order of {threshold}, or add a small handling fee to orders below it.
tests.success: Orders under {threshold}: from {small_share}% to {target_share}% of orders

leaks.only_if: extra cross-border fees can be derived from the fee data; otherwise skip this leak
leaks.name: Orders from abroad cost you more
leaks.why: Payments from other countries usually carry extra fees, so the same item earns you less.

questions.text: Do buyers abroad pay the same as buyers at home?

tests.do: Build the extra fee into the price or the shipping for orders from abroad.
tests.success: You keep as much per order from abroad as from home
tests.target_rule: kept share abroad >= kept share at home

tests.do: Check that your price for buyers abroad covers the extra fee shown here.
tests.success: You keep as much per order from abroad as from home
tests.target_rule: kept share abroad >= kept share at home

leaks.name: One item makes almost half your money
leaks.why: If it stops selling, half your income goes with it.

tests.do: Make one new variation of {top_group} this month.

leaks.name: This item loses money
leaks.why: After materials, shipping and fees, each sale of {item} leaves you with less than you put in.

tests.do: Raise the price of {item} to at least {break_even_price}, or stop making it.
tests.success: Every item keeps money after costs

leaks.name: Fewer new people find you
leaks.why: {new_share}% of your sales come from first-time buyers. When fewer arrive, everything shrinks.

questions.text: Where do new buyers usually find you?

tests.do: Post your best seller 3 times this week, each with a different first line, and note which one brings orders.
Refresh the photos and titles of your 3 best items.
Ask your last 5 happy buyers to send your link to one friend.
Ask every buyer this month one question: where did you find me?
tests.success: An answer from most of this month's buyers

leaks.name: Subscription payments fail quietly
leaks.why: When a payment fails, the subscription can stop without anyone noticing. A short message often brings people back.

tests.do: Message the {n_failed} subscribers whose payment failed, with a link to update their payment.
